samples: This program manages a small SQLite inventory database: it opens or creates an `items` table, records deliveries by increasing an item’s quantity, and finds items whose stock is at or below their reorder level. Its `main` function applies one hardcoded delivery to a specific SKU, then prints either “nothing to reorder” or a list of low-stock items with their current and reorder quantities. It also includes a replayable test that seeds sample data and verifies that only the truly low-stock item is reported after the delivery.

This program manages a small SQLite-backed inventory table, creating it if needed, recording deliveries for existing items, and querying items whose stock is at or below their reorder level. Its `main` routine opens `data/inventory.db`, adds 500 units to SKU `BOLT-10`, then prints either “nothing to reorder” or a list of low-stock items with their current and reorder quantities. It also includes a replayable test that seeds a test database and verifies that only the truly low-stock item is reported after the delivery update.

This program manages a small SQLite inventory database: it creates the items table if needed, records deliveries by increasing stock for a given SKU, and queries items whose quantity is at or below their reorder level. Its main entry point always adds 500 units to one hardcoded item, then prints either “nothing to reorder” or a list of low-stock items with their current and reorder quantities. It also includes a replayable test that seeds a test database and verifies that only the truly low-stock item is reported after the delivery update.

This program manages a small SQLite-backed inventory table, with functions to open the database, list items that are at or below their reorder level, and record incoming deliveries for an existing SKU. Its main routine opens a fixed database file, adds 500 units to one hardcoded item, then prints any items that still need reordering, or says nothing needs reorder if the list is empty. It also includes a replayable test that seeds a test database and verifies that low-stock reporting works as expected.

Its main routine opens a fixed database file, adds 500 units to one hardcoded item, then prints any items that still need reordering, or says nothing needs reorder if the list is empty. It also includes a test that seeds a temporary database and verifies that low-stock items are reported correctly after a delivery update.
